E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, not measured treatment performance.

weightPotential.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–17 (marker POTASSIUM SORBATE @18, resolved and plausible on all three §3.1.1 limbs) — the cohort's second-longest credited segment; an ingredient-informed matching prior, not a prediction of visible finish.
weightPotential.rationale: CHANGED under v0.3 (E4, applied uniformly per E6, 2026-09-14): `moderate` → `low`. E4 deleted the structural fatty-alcohol conjunct from the leanness test and E6 rules the restated test applies uniformly across the cohort. This record satisfies all three remaining conjuncts on the FULL list, not merely above the marker: no R4b heavy lipid (the sole lipid, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL @17, is a conventional plant triglyceride and sits in the lexicon's MID band), no occlusive silicone stack (no silicone at any rank), and a single cationic species (DISTEAROYLETHYL DIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4). The v0.2 record called this the cohort's most striking refusal of `low`, because the pack's own 'ohne zu beschweren' positioning corroborated a lightness the anchor would not grant. It grants it now, on formula evidence, with the claim as corroboration it does not need. E2 ceiling: weight deposition potential, never measured finish.
evidenceSignals: CONJUNCT 1 — no R4b heavy lipid above the marker: SATISFIED. HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL @17 is the formula's only lipid of any class. Lexicon family 3 places it with the conventional plant triglycerides in the MID weight band (heavy = butters, Ricinus, petrolatum, hydrogenated fats, lanolin), so it is R4a and cannot carry the heavy-lipid core. No butter, no hydrogenated fat and no occlusive hydrocarbon at ANY rank: the conjunct holds on the full 21-entry list

CONJUNCT 2 — no occlusive silicone stack above the tail: SATISFIED, absolutely. No silicone species at any rank — a NATRUE-certified Naturkosmetik formula. The occlusive-stack completer needs two silicone species or a dimethicone/dimethiconol pair; there is not one

CONJUNCT 3 — a single cationic species: SATISFIED on the above-tail segment AND on the full list. DISTEAROYLETHYL DIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4 is the only S1-family species anywhere in the formula; the tail holds only POTASSIUM SORBATE @18, PARFUM @19 and two declared allergens, so no cationic is hidden by the marker cut. This is the difference between this record and #07/#09, whose conjunct-3 counts depend on the above-tail scope (AP-07-CATIONICSCOPE)

CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2 and BEHENYL ALCOHOL @5 — the two long-chain fatty alcohols that refused this product `low` under v0.1 and v0.2. E4 deletes the conjunct they failed: lexicon family 2 records a structurant fatty alcohol at rank 2 as near-universal in this category, so a leanness test failing on it was failing on the category baseline

tail marker POTASSIUM SORBATE @18, resolved and `plausible: true` — seventeen credited entries carry the entire architecture and all outrank it. §9.2 makes `low` unavailable on an unreadable segment; here the segment is the cohort's most readable

`moderate` does not apply, and this is the value that MOVED. Under v0.1 the cetearyl top-three cut refused it; under v0.2 R4's thin-fatty-base test kept the same cut and refused it again, which the v0.2 record escalated as the second and more striking instance of AP-07-LOWUNREACHABLE — more striking because here the exact-product positioning explicitly claimed lightness and the formula corroborated it, and the anchor still said no. WHY-NOT-ADJACENT on the one term that could flip this: conjunct 1 turns on HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL @17 being R4a rather than R4b. That is lexicon-backed rather than a reviewer judgment — family 3 lists sunflower oil among the triglycerides/plant oils and puts 'conventional plant triglycerides' in the mid band, reserving heavy for butters, Ricinus, petrolatum, hydrogenated fats and lanolin. The evidence note that singles sunflower oil out (P-3, Rele & Mohile) does so for NON-penetration, which is a penetration finding and not a weight one, and §9.2 reads weight from lipid class and load. Were it R4b, conjunct 1 would fail and the value would be `moderate` — but nothing in the lexicon or the evidence base supports that reading.

COUNTING SCOPE is NOT a live caveat here, unlike on #07 and #09: conjunct 3 holds on the full list, so the above-tail counting scope §9.2 flags as its own unruled addition does no work on this record and could not move the value.

§9.2 conflict fallback checked and NOT engaged: it applies to a formula-only `high` contradicted by lightness positioning. Here the formula and the positioning AGREE — 'ohne zu beschweren' meets a `low` value — so the asymmetry the v0.2 record complained about (no mechanism for a formula-plus-claim lightness reading the anchor refuses) has no subject any more. `weight_high_conflict` cannot fire on a `low` value.

Confidence `high`, and this is the cohort's only `high`-confidence weight value — stated explicitly because it is a departure from the surrounding records. §4.1's bar is 'exact complete input, no material gap, converging independent signals, reasonable unknowns would not move the value', and §9.2's own rule asks for the full anchor pattern on a resolved and plausible marker with no positioning conflict. All four hold: a brand-direct verbatim fetch of the exact SKU (identityState `verified`), a seventeen-entry credited segment, three conjuncts that each hold on the full list, and positioning that corroborates rather than conflicts. The only identified unknown — the sunflower oil's weight band — is lexicon-settled. Contrast #07, #09 and #12, each capped at `moderate` for a named and different reason.

Under v0.1 and v0.2 both sat against a profile value of `moderate` and the divergence was recorded as the anchor's rather than the evidence's; under v0.3 the graded readings and the anchor agree.

A `high`-confidence value on an anchor that became reachable on 2026-09-14 and has no calibration behind it. The two statements are compatible — confidence measures classification robustness on this record, not the anchor's calibrated accuracy (§4.1, §15) — but a reviewer who reads cohort confidence as a proxy for method maturity should see it named here rather than infer it.

The weight move does NOT move the focus on this record, and that is E6's doing rather than a coincidence: this product carries `body_lightness_potential: likely_preserving`, so under the deleted §9.5.2 step-3 route a `low` weight would have displaced the `moisture` headline with `lightness`. E6 removes the value from the vocabulary, so the headline stands on its own D5 cluster evidence. See the primaryFocus re-check.

A conventional formula with early Parfum would have less of its list read. The tail rule is not weight-neutral across formulation philosophies, and this record benefits from that.
limitations: A soft preference with a stated reason, never an exclusion. Fine-hair flattening is a fit mismatch, not a hair-type law (§9.2 wording rule); `low` is a desired-finish and dosage prior, never a claim that the product is weak.
An ingredient-informed matching prior at E2, never a prediction about visible body or finish.

careDirection.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–17; comparative care emphasis, never an assertion about a user's protein or moisture state (G6).
careDirection.rationale: This is the cohort's only genuinely substantive `balanced`: three distinct hydrolyzed proteins at consecutive ranks 7–9 satisfy the material R5 route on both of its legs, and five distinct qualifying humectants above the tail satisfy the humectant-cluster leg of the balanced test — not the loose S3 lipid leg that carried #04 and #05. Both sides of the value are real. E2 ceiling: comparative emphasis, not a delivered outcome.
evidenceSignals: HYDROLYZED CORN PROTEIN (7), HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN (8), HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN (9) — three distinct qualifying R5 species above the tail, at consecutive ranks

GLYCERIN (3), BETAINE (6), SODIUM LACTATE (12), SODIUM HYALURONATE (13), ALOE BARBADENSIS LEAF JUICE POWDER (14) — five distinct qualifying humectant-class members above the tail, four of them non-glycerin
ARGININE (rank 11) — free amino acid, deliberately EXCLUDED from the humectant cluster (not on R9's list) and excluded from R5 by the mask delta
HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL (17) — the single lipid; S3 is NOT satisfied, so the lipid leg of the balanced test is unavailable here

LACTIC ACID (10) / SODIUM LACTATE (12) — a buffer pair; C3's amidoamine-neutraliser reading does NOT apply because the cationic is a permanent esterquat, so Sodium Lactate is counted as a humectant on its own merits
careDirection.derivation: §9.3 material-R5 test satisfied on leg (a) (three distinct species above the tail) and independently on leg (b) (a qualifying species at above-tail rank 7, inside the first eight). Then the `balanced` test: material R5 route AND (a qualifying humectant cluster of ≥3 distinct humectants above the tail with ≥2 non-glycerin, OR S3). The humectant cluster leg succeeds with five members and four non-glycerin; the S3 leg fails with one lipid. → `balanced`, earned on the humectant leg.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `balanced`: both conjuncts hold, and the second holds on the strict humectant-cluster leg rather than the loose lipid leg. D6 reserves `balanced` for a substantive mixed protein-plus-moisture architecture; three proteins and five humectants above the tail is that architecture.
`protein` does not apply: the humectant leg is substantive and independent, so this is not a protein-dominant formula.
`moisture` does not apply: three hydrolyzed proteins at ranks 7–9 is a dominant protein-film route by any reading, and `moisture` is defined as the coherent direction WITHOUT one.

Aloe counted once and never as a strong member, per lexicon family 7's 'reconstituted powder at trace level' caution — the source list says 'Leaf Juice Powder' explicitly. Even discounting Aloe entirely, the cluster is four members with three non-glycerin and still clears.

Re-checked under v0.2 (R6). The value is unchanged and its reading is now recorded explicitly: `balanced_reading: both_substantive`. Both legs are substantive above the tail — a material R5 route (HYDROLYZED CORN @7, WHEAT @8, SOY @9) AND a qualifying humectant cluster meeting §9.5.3 criterion 1 (GLYCERIN @3, BETAINE @6, SODIUM LACTATE @12, SODIUM HYALURONATE @13, ALOE @14: five distinct, four non-glycerin). R6 deletes the lipid-leg path into `balanced`, which is what moves #04 and #05 to `protein`; this product never used that path and is unaffected. Reading (b) is unavailable at clause 1 (a protein anchor is present).
counterSignals: D4 heavy-protein-payload counter-signal FIRES (three distinct R5 species above the tail), binding confidence to `moderate` (§13 effect 2). Confidence would otherwise have been `high` — resolved tail marker, brand-direct verbatim source, unambiguous route separation.

Arginine's exclusion is a judgment: lexicon family 5b allows free amino acids 'at most a very weak contribution to the humectant cluster when several appear above the tail with no plausible neutraliser role', and here there IS no amidoamine to neutralise. I excluded it because R9's enumeration does not list it. Including it would raise the cluster to six and change nothing.
limitations: INCI discloses no molecular weight; P-5's mechanics evidence is entirely MW-conditional, so the three-protein cluster supports 'a protein film route is present' and nothing about strength or breakage.

Banned vocabulary observed: no 'protein overload' language, and no 'hygral fatigue' reading of the humectant cluster (lexicon family 7: an unestablished construct that must never appear as a rule, a warning, or copy).

exact-product positioning used as the tie-breaker, verbatim: product name 'Intense Hydration'; claims 'Feuchtigkeitsbooster für trockenes Haar', 'schützt langanhaltend vor dem Austrocknen'. The competing claim leg ('3-Fach Protein Komplex') is recorded as the losing candidate's corroboration
primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: the protein cluster is one M2 observation and the humectant cluster one M5 observation — genuinely disjoint, and neither is M1. Step 3: `repair` clears its protein-film disjunct. Step 4: `moisture` independently clears all four §9.5.3 criteria, including criterion 2 in both its baseline sentence and its R5 lipid-led limbs. Both candidates therefore cleared their own thresholds on the formula, which is the definition of `dual_supported`. §9.5.1 as scoped by R7 then breaks the tie on exact-product positioning: `moisture` primary, `repair` secondary.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moisture` as primary: a formula-supported candidate, chosen over an equally formula-supported candidate by exact-product positioning on a genuinely `dual_supported` verdict. R7's discipline observed exhaustively — the claim chose between two candidates the formula already supports; it created no third candidate, lowered no threshold, upgraded no `nonspecific` evidence, and substituted for no corroboration leg.

`repair` does not take the primary slot — the change from v0.1. Under v0.1 the §9.5.2 step order alone decided it, and the claim leg had nothing to do; R7 states that the order decides which routes are tested first, not which of two cleared routes wins. `repair` keeps a secondary slot, so both endpoints remain on the record.

§9.5.3 criterion 3 is satisfied in the direction that matters here: no RICHER special-purpose route wins. `repair` cleared, but the tie-break assigned it the secondary slot, and criterion 3's own text contemplates exactly this pairing.

R5's lipid-led disqualifier was tested and does NOT fire: one R4a mid-band oil at rank 17, no R4b heavy lipid above the marker. This formula is the opposite of lipid-led — it is the cohort's leanest humectant-forward architecture after #09.
`smoothing` does not apply: its claim ('glättet die Haarstruktur & wirkt Frizz entgegen') has no architecture behind it — no silicone, no substantive polymer, one lipid at rank 17.
`general` does not apply: two differentiators cleared.

RE-CHECKED under v0.3 (E4/E6), value UNCHANGED at `moisture` — and on this record the re-check is not a formality. `weight_potential` moved to `low`, and `body_lightness_potential` has read `likely_preserving` since v0.1, which are exactly the two conditions the DELETED §9.5.2 step-3 `lightness` route required. Under the v0.3 text as it stood before E6, this product's headline would have been displaced from `moisture` to `lightness` by a weight ruling, with no focus rule changing and no focus evidence moving. E6 removes `lightness` from the vocabulary and deletes the route, so step 3 now tests three routes — `repair` (clears, and takes the secondary slot on the R7 tie-break), `curl_support` (blocked) and `color_care` (blocked) — and step 4's D5 guard decides the headline on the humectant cluster, exactly as it did under v0.1 and v0.2. Every other rule that could touch this field was checked against the moved weight value: `shine` §9.5.4 criterion 1 reads lipid load, not the weight value, and fails for want of any alignment-oriented R2/R3 route; `curl_support` reads slip plus weight/body architecture and is blocked on a single cationic with no polymer; the §9.5.3 guard never reads weight. No rule forces a move.
counterSignals: Confidence stays `moderate`: §9.5.3's confidence rule requires 'no competing route' for `high`, and `repair` is a live competing route sitting in the secondary slot.

'verbessert die Kämmbarkeit ohne zu beschweren' is a lightness claim. RESTATED under v0.3: it is still recorded and still creates nothing, but the reason has changed. Under v0.1 and v0.2 it met a `moderate` weight value and no §9.2 conflict arose; under v0.3 it meets `weight_potential: low`, so formula and positioning now agree and there is nothing to reconcile. `weight_high_conflict` cannot fire on a `low` value in any case, and the claim reached no focus field in either revision — E6 having removed the only focus route that read leanness.

The tie-break is claim-dependent by construction. A reviewer who read the verdict as `repair_supported` rather than `dual_supported` would not reach the tie-break at all — but the cluster's independent clearance of all four D5 criteria is what makes the verdict dual, and that is a formula finding.

The headline is stable under v0.3 only because of E6. This is the clearest cohort instance of the effect E6 was ruled against: a Feuchtigkeitsmaske with a five-member humectant cluster, whose D5 guard clears with room, would have had its forced headline spent on a deposition property the `weight_potential` field already reports. Recorded so the dependency is visible rather than implicit — if `lightness` were ever restored to the vocabulary, this record moves.
limitations: Wording rule (D5, binding) observed absolutely: this record says 'humectant-forward comparative direction' and never 'hydrates', 'proven hydration', 'moisturizes' or 'restores moisture balance' — notwithstanding that the product's own name is 'Intense Hydration'.
Adapter boundary: `moisture` has no `functional_benefits` counterpart and reaches production only via `balance_direction`. No projection is authorized here.

focusCareVerdict.note: Unchanged verdict, resolved tie (R7, 2026-09-14). The formula genuinely supports both directions: three distinct hydrolyzed proteins at ranks 7–9 (M2) and five distinct humectants across four families above the tail (M5), on disjoint mechanisms with almost no M1 richness to confuse either with. This is the cohort's only `dual_supported` verdict. Under v0.1 the claim leg was recorded as eligible but NOT applied, because §9.5.2's step order had already resolved the primary slot to `repair`; AP-08-TIEBREAK escalated the conflict. R7 settles it: the step order decides which routes are tested first, not which of two cleared routes wins, and on a genuinely dual verdict exact-product positioning may break the tie at any step and in either direction, including which candidate takes primary and which takes a secondary slot. Claim text applied as tie-breaker, verbatim: product name 'Intense Hydration'; claim 'Feuchtigkeitsbooster für trockenes Haar'. Competing focus that lost the primary slot: `repair`, which retains the secondary slot.
